rubrics_metrics.name: Vatican Holy Office ruling on news vendors selling Communist publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Catholic vendors who 'knowingly and freely' sell Communist newspapers must be refused the sacraments; allowances are made for news vendors 'under effective coercion' to handle Communist publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Holy Office explained that in some cities union organizations may coerce vendors to carry Communist papers; if a vendor can, without grave danger to himself, avoid selling the prohibited papers, then selling them is deemed 'knowingly and freely' and sanctions (refusal of sacraments) apply. If the vendor finds himself under 'effective coercion' material cooperation can be tolerated provided his obligation of conscience to limit such co-operation 'as far as possible' is observed. The reply noted this is a matter of local circumstances ('a thing... in which the news vendor himself is expert') and does not attempt to list every situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal decree on excommunication and denial of sacraments for Communist supporters
rubrics_metrics.description: A historic Papal decree excommunicates Catholics who 'militantly defend Communism' and denies the Holy Sacraments to those who 'publish, read or disseminate books, newspapers or leaflets in support of Communist doctrine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Holy Office's clarification to Cardinal Ruffini reiterated the scope of the July decree: militant defense or active dissemination/support of Communist doctrine is subject to excommunication and sacramental denial. The Holy Office applied the decree to the practical question of news vendors, distinguishing voluntary, knowing cooperation (punishable) from coerced material cooperation (permitted with moral restrictions). The ruling was issued in response to concerns about union pressure on vendors and the difficulty of distribution in some cities.
